text: Girlfriends is an American sitcom created by Mara Brock Akil that premiered on UPN on September 11, 2000, airing for its first six seasons until May 8, 2006. On October 1, 2006, the series moved to The CW, a network formed by the merger of UPN and The WB, where it aired for two additional seasons before being cancelled on February 11, 2008. The show initially aired on UPN on Mondays at 9:00/8:00c, and after moving to The CW, it was scheduled on Sundays at 8:00/7:00c, leading to a decline in ratings. On October 9, 2006, Girlfriends, along with other African-American programming on The CW, returned to Mondays, resuming its original time slot. Due to the 2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike, the final episodes produced aired on February 11, 2008. The CW had planned to move the series to Sunday nights, but on February 13, 2008, it announced the cancellation after eight seasons, citing low ratings and the high cost of restarting production. A retrospective episode was being developed to conclude the series, but was scrapped after The CW offered the actors only half of their usual episodic salaries, which they collectively rejected. The 2006 episode "The Game" features guest star Tia Mowry as Joan's cousin Melanie Barnett, an aspiring medical student who wants to leave her studies to follow her athlete boyfriend to San Diego; this episode launched the spin-off series The Game, which was cancelled by The CW. In April 2010, BET picked up The Game, which aired new episodes until its August 5, 2015 finale. When The Game's fourth season premiered in 2011, it drew 7.7 million viewers, making it the most watched sitcom premiere in cable television history at the time. In November 2021, a revival spin-off of Girlfriends was picked up and released on Paramount+, serving as a direct sequel to the original series and marketed as a refreshed reboot (chronicled as season 10), continuing the overall season count. The new series picks up years after the 2015 finale, shifting the setting to Las Vegas and introducing new protagonists: Tasha Mack, a woman of color sports agent; her son Malik Wright, who struggles with mental health while making key decisions in his sports career; and Brittany Pitts, who faces serious financial hardships and seeks independence from her Pro-Football father Jason Pitts' image and inheritance. The reboot also introduces new characters to the storyline and has received favorable reviews from media outlets. The complete series is available to stream on The CW's free digital-only network, CW Seed, and began streaming on Netflix on September 11, 2020, to mark the show's 20th anniversary.
